goal: A best practice it makes produces deliverables that achieve their user's purpose.

parts.what: What the user achieves with the deliverable.
The deliverable's parts that meet the goal: each part and what it holds, in the order the user meets them; how they are written out is decided when the deliverable is made.

Questions that check, by the essence, whether the deliverable achieves the goal: what each part, each dependency among parts and the whole bring the user, each asked so it is answered yes or no, in the order the builder thinks them.
For each question, in the benefits' order, the best way of thinking that meets its essence, and steps only where the thinking alone does not lead the builder, with the grounds where they have worked.

benefits.what: Reading the goal, does one see a single thing the user achieves with the deliverable?
Looking at the parts, does the builder know what to write in which part, and in what order?
Do the parts hold, neither more nor less, the parts the goal needs?
With each question, can one who judges the deliverable tell whether that part serves the user?
For each part, each dependency among parts and the whole, is there a question asking whether it serves the user?
Following the way of thinking and the steps, can the builder make the content the question asks for?
Does every question have, in the benefits' order, a way of thinking that meets its essence?
Does a deliverable made by this best practice, and passed, let its user achieve their purpose?

practices.thinking: The goal is what the user is trying to get done, seen from where they stand, not what the deliverable holds.
steps: Name the one who uses the deliverable.
Ask what they are trying to get done when they reach for it.
Write that as one sentence with them as its subject, free of what the deliverable holds or how it is made.
Ask whether two readers would name the same achievement from it; where they would name two, keep the one the other serves.

practices.thinking: The parts are learned from good and poor deliverables of the kind, each part written as what its user needs from it rather than as one way some deliverables give it, and laid out in the order its user meets it.
steps: Gather good and poor deliverables of the kind.
List what the good ones hold that their user uses toward the goal.
For each such thing that is one way of doing it, such as a place, a file or a name, ask what its user gets from it, and keep that instead.
Make each such thing a part, saying what it holds.
Order the parts as the user meets them.

grounds.quote: Look at models. Review examples of good and poor work on a project like the one your students are about to undertake.

practices.thinking: Each part is there because the goal needs it, and what the goal needs is found by imagining a deliverable that has every part and still fails its user.
steps: For each part, say what the user could not do toward the goal without it; cut a part with no answer.
Imagine a deliverable that has every part and still fails its user, and make what it lacks a part.
Repeat until no such deliverable can be imagined.

practices.thinking: A question asks whether the user gets what they need, not whether a sign of good work is there, so it cannot be met in the letter while the user goes without.
steps: Name who uses what the question asks of, and the moment they use it.
Ask what they need from it there toward the goal.
Write the question as whether they get that, answered yes or no.
Ask whether a deliverable could meet the question's words while the user still does not get it; if so, rewrite the question to ask the getting itself.
Ask whether the question says more than whether the work is good; if not, name what the user gets.
Have two evaluators judge one real deliverable by the question; where they differ, rewrite the question until it is read one way.

practices.thinking: The questions are complete when no deliverable can pass them all and still fail its user, and each need is asked in one place.
steps: List each part, each pair of parts where one depends on another, and the whole.
Give each one its question.
Merge questions that would fail the same deliverables for the same reason, keeping a key one on its own.
Imagine a deliverable that passes every question and still fails its user, and add the question that would fail it.
Judge real deliverables their users found short; where one passes, add or mend the question that should have failed it.

practices.thinking: A way of making is taken from where it has met the essence before and kept only once it meets it here; the way of thinking carries it, and a step is there only for what the thinking alone does not lead the builder to.
steps: For the essence the question holds, find how good deliverables met it: guides, studies and examples.
Write the way of thinking in one sentence.
Write a step only for what the way of thinking alone does not lead the builder to, one action each, in order.
Where a step or a source names one way of doing it, such as a place, a file or a tool, write what that way achieves, so a project that achieves it another way keeps its own.
Add as grounds the words of the sources, quoted from the pages opened, each with its page's title and link; cut a step that no source holds and the way of thinking already implies.
Make one real deliverable by the way, and judge it by the question; where it stays no, mend the way.

practices.thinking: Every essence of every question has its way, so the builder never meets a question with nothing to go by.
steps: Order the questions in the order the builder thinks them, so that one is answered before those that build on it.
Give each question one practice, in that order, and make one by Q6's way for a question that has none.

practices.thinking: Only a deliverable made and used shows whether the whole works, and the user's own verdict is what a verdict by the questions is set against.
steps: Make one real deliverable by the practices, and pass it by the benefits.
Have its user, or an AI holding what the user wants, use it for the goal.
Set the user's verdict against the evaluator's.
Trace each difference to the goal, the parts, a question or a practice, and mend it there.
Go through again with the next real deliverable.
